originality.rationale: Substantive content comparison, not timestamp/search-count. Nearest results: (i) Steinberg 2011 (arXiv:1107.3051) proves Cerny upper bound (n-1)^2=49 for prime-cycle one-cluster automata — upper-bound only, no exact n=8 k=5 maximum, no extremal witness, no census; this work is complementary lower-bound/exact side (M>=34 + exact perm-subslice max 34) inside Steinberg's regime. (ii) Kisielewicz-Kowalski-Szykula experiments / Szykula database target unrestricted and Cerny-cyclic automata and report slowly synchronizing series, but do not isolate the (n=8,binary,one-cluster,5-cycle) slice nor its maximum; methods and slice disjoint. (iii) Volkov survey lists general bounds (Cerny 49, Kari Eulerian, Trahtman/Rystsov aperiodic 28, monotonic) and known series (Cerny, Kari, Ananichev) — no tight prime-5-cycle n=8 value; confirms gap. Structural disjointness checked: witness is not Cerny (would need rt 49; a is not 8-cycle), not Kari Eulerian (a indegrees 2,1,1,1,1,1,1,0, not Eulerian), b is an 8-cycle so swapped-role view still does not match Cerny merging shape. Live literature fetches failed in sandbox (arxiv 502, wikipedia transport error, curl TLS SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL) as the draft itself discloses; no priority claim is made and none is needed — novelty rests on checkable artifacts and the absence of this exact table from standard bounds/surveys by content. Residual risk of a missed prior table remains but does not defeat substantive delta.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later. Not textbook: Cerny open since 1964, exact small-n maxima for structured slices are active research. Not parameter substitution: 5-cycle one-cluster restriction is qualitative (Steinberg theorem regime, excludes 8-cycle Cerny shape, changes combinatorics), not n=7->8. Not tiny epsilon gain: 34 exceeds the aperiodic universal bound 28 by 6 (21% over) and attains ~69% of Cerny 49, proving prime-cycle restriction still permits super-aperiodic slowness — a regime-crossing threshold with landscape meaning between 28 and 49. Not unexplained enumeration: every catalog entry carries shortest word + forward/reverse BFS distances + replay check, plus distribution histograms (mixed 484k, perm 564k) and comparison to Steinberg/Cerny/aperiodic bounds; exhaustive perm-b census (564480 automata, exact max 34) is a complete enumerative theorem for a natural subcase (permutation letter), with reusable stdlib verifier (<2s). Fallback anticipated >=25 catalog if >=32 missed; actual 34 exceeds the motivating >=32 threshold. Honest scope (full M not pinned, non-perm >34 possible) preserves value as lower bound + benchmark.
